findings.title: Budget rule contradicts tool loosening
findings.problem: The system prompt says the budget stays the limit, but rag.search silently raises or removes the budget when loosening, so the two sources give conflicting budget behaviour.
findings.proof: A budget stays the limit when the shopper invites going over it; the reply names how to raise it.
findings.fix: State in the system prompt that a budget may be loosened by the tool (raised 25% or removed) only when the reply reports the loosened price, and align the schema's loosening order with that rule.

findings.title: Loosening order repeated in schema and prompt
findings.problem: The loosening sequence appears in the tool description and is restated in the Search rules, so the two copies can drift apart.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found:
findings.fix: Keep the loosening order only in the tool description and reference it from the system prompt in one clause.

findings.title: Fixed-sentence cap is ambiguous
findings.problem: The reply is capped at three fixed sentences, yet the product-answer rule says all of them are also on screen, so the limit for on-screen text is unclear.
findings.proof: Before a product answer two are spoken in short form, a third if time allows; all are on screen.
findings.fix: Define whether the three-sentence cap applies to spoken text only, or to on-screen text as well.

findings.title: No code guard on names and addresses
findings.problem: Names and street addresses are left to a model-side rule with no code screen, unlike e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers, which are masked before any model sees them.
findings.fix: Add a code-level screen or a named-entity check for names and street addresses in the input screen, and state in the system prompt which step enforces it.

findings.title: Pipeline Router prose is verbose
findings.problem: The Router step carries a long re-reading rule that could be stated in a few words without losing the behaviour.
findings.proof: A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model for a buried product request;
findings.fix: Reduce the Router's re-reading rule to one short sentence stating the trigger and the outcome.

findings.title: Loosening rules restated in the Search paragraph
findings.problem: The never-loosened list is repeated in the system prompt even though the schema already states it.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated never-loosened list from the system prompt and point to the tool description.

findings.title: Fixed-reply texts are duplicated in short form
findings.problem: Several fixed replies appear once in full and again in a shortened list, so the same wording is stored twice.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Store each reply once with a short-form field, or generate the short forms from the full texts in code.

findings.title: Two limits for the same spoken reply
findings.problem: The spoken summary is limited to 15 seconds in the goal and to 45 words in the rule checks, so the reader has two units for one constraint.
findings.proof: a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds
findings.fix: State the limit once, in words, and derive the other from it in a single clause.

findings.title: Fixture results not flagged for the Answerer
findings.problem: The system prompt never tells the Answerer or Critic that fixture results name fake stores, so an offline sample could be presented as a real source.
findings.proof: `provider` names what answered; "fixture" is a recorded offline sample (stores named "Example ..."), used when no search key is configured.
findings.fix: Add a rule in the system prompt that a result from the fixture provider must be labelled as sample data and never cited as a real store.

findings.title: Closest-alternative rule is undefined
findings.problem: The abstention path allows a closest alternative but does not define how it is chosen or what it may claim.
findings.proof: with at most one closest alternative from the evidence within the hard limits.
findings.fix: Define the selection criterion for the closest alternative and state that its claims follow the same rules as any other row.

findings.title: Router defaults to search when in doubt
findings.problem: The Router is told to default to a product search when in doubt, which can pull an injected clause into a search if the input screen misses it.
findings.proof: intent (a product search when in doubt)
findings.fix: Require the input screen's removal list to be applied before the default, and state that doubt does not override a removed clause.

findings.title: Injection defence relies on the MCP server alone
findings.problem: Instruction-like text is removed by the server, with no code-side check on the model's inputs to catch any that gets through.
findings.proof: The MCP server removes instruction-like text from tool results (catalog listings and web results) before any model sees it;
findings.fix: Add a code check on tool results for instruction-like patterns before they enter the fenced prompt, and log any match.
